Subject: Recap: Pilot success map & proposed 4-week evaluation (Celestify)

Hi Rachel / Samir — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a concrete pilot proposal so we can move to scheduling. I captured the bits we discussed and added a suggested timeline, success metrics, and owners. Feedback welcome.

High-level goal
- Validate integration of Redwood Inference into Celestify's relevance pipeline and measure end-to-end latency and retrieval quality at production-like scale.

Proposed success criteria (what you tell your execs)
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 250 ms on the test harness
- Throughput: sustain 10 qps with <15% tailbackpressure on our staging pool
- Quality: reranking precision (NDCG@10) uplift >= 6% vs current baseline OR embedding recall >= 0.78 on the provided eval set
- Cost: token-level unit cost estimate and projected monthly run-rate for 100k queries/day

4-week pilot outline (shallow -> deep)
- Week 0 (prep, 3 days): NDA, sample data handoff, account + cloud access, baseline capture (current pipeline metrics)
- Week 1 (integration): connector + ingestion, sample prompt set, run small-scale baseline tests
- Week 2 (scale + tuning): throughput tuning (batching/quantization), KV cache tuning, run full eval suite
- Week 3 (finalize + handoff): results, ROI/cost report, incremental recommendations and acceptance review

Ownership
- Redwood: Laura (PM) — project owner, onboarding cadence; Logan (Eng) — technical lead for integration and tuning
- Celestify: Rachel — product owner; Samir — engineering lead

Immediate next steps
1) If agreed, we'll send an updated pilot scope workbook (attached: celestify_pilot_scope.xlsx) and a short SOW for signature.
2) Please share a sample of the evaluation dataset and an ingest endpoint or S3 details (we'll treat data per our standard controls).
3) Tentative kickoff window: Oct 26–30 (please confirm availability).

Attachments: celestify_pilot_scope.xlsx (workbook with tasks, milestones), sample_prompt_set.jsonl (example prompts).

Thanks — happy to jump on 15–20m to walk through the workbook.
